body:
Chief: read-only review against my prior blockers. ALL THREE ADR REQUIREMENTS ARE MET, and one of them you met harder than I asked.

R1 -- a relation the compiler cannot derive is ABSENT AND RECORDED, never present at a default weight. Met, and this is the one: 'multi-situation input now records a DiscourseTrajectory gap, leaves the trajectory empty, and blocks promotion instead of calling the current ABSENCE-ERASING DERIVE PATH.' You applied your own label to your own compiler and then chose to block rather than derive. Blocking promotion is stronger than recording a gap and continuing, and I did not ask for it.

R2 -- the receipt is part of the ARTIFACT, not a log line. Met. DerivationReceipt plus gaps inside candidate identity means the absence travels with the value and survives serialization, which is the whole point.

R3 -- absence-erasing derivation as a review category. Met by use rather than by declaration, which is better.

ALSO RIGHT, and these are the ones that would have been easy to skip: provider values no longer carrying EpistemicStatus; a deterministic pure-Scala fixture provider that is HONESTLY NAMED rather than handwritten literals wrapped in Agent provenance; and rejecting non-Asserted modalities outright because the first slice cannot represent child contexts, rather than silently flattening them.

NOW THE ONE THING I WANT STATED PRECISELY, AND IT IS NOT A CRITICISM -- you already said it correctly and I want it to stay said.

'raw-source/raw-recall vertical Passed 1/1' is MECHANICAL REACHABILITY ON ONE SENTENCE WITH A DETERMINISTIC FIXTURE PROVIDER. It is not a real transcript reaching an answered research question. You wrote 'claims one-sentence mechanical reachability only' and that phrasing must survive into the commit message and the ADR, because it is exactly the kind of sentence that gets compressed to 'the vertical passes' by the third person who repeats it -- and I would be the one repeating it to the owner.

WHAT IT DOES PROVE IS LARGE AND I DO NOT WANT TO UNDERSELL IT EITHER: the arrow exists. Until today nothing produced a NarrativeGraph plus NarrativeHierarchy from a SurfaceAtlas -- not an implementation, not a stub, not a provider trait -- and the path from raw text to a signature was severed at that joint. A one-sentence case that runs the whole way through is the difference between a severed path and a narrow one. Narrow is a scaling problem. Severed was not.

NO GATE VERDICT REQUESTED AND NONE GIVEN. When you do want one, gate from the MERGE BASE rather than main -- main has moved five times since your base (D2, my SourceView law, ADR 0004, B1+B2 which changed RecallSignature.compute to return Either, and the absorb-tolerance fix). THAT FOURTH ONE WILL TOUCH YOU: if your vertical calls RecallSignature.compute, its return type changed under you at e7a5ba0 and your rebase will not be clean.

I am running a full-main audit right now for exactly that reason.
